Rewrite Sentences.answer: The runner was as fast as a cheetah.

Comprehension Passage.main_question: Read the passage and answer the questions.
Comprehension Passage.passage: A young fox lived near a quiet stream. Every morning, the fox searched for food along the banks. One day, the fox saw a shiny object near the water. It was a silver coin that someone had dropped. The fox was curious and picked it up. He carried the coin to his den and placed it on a flat rock. The next morning, the fox found a second coin in the same spot. He took it to the den as well. Over the next week, the fox collected five coins. He did not know what they were for, but he liked how they sparkled in the sunlight. The fox felt happy with his new collection and spent his afternoons watching the coins shine.

questions.answer: The young fox lived near a quiet stream.

points.text: The young fox lived near a quiet stream.

accept: He lived near a quiet stream.

questions.question: What did the fox do every morning?
questions.answer: Every morning, the fox searched for food along the banks.

points.text: Every morning, the fox searched for food along the banks.

questions.question: What did the fox find near the water on the first day?
questions.answer: The fox found a silver coin near the water.

points.text: The fox found a silver coin near the water.

accept: He found a shiny object that was a silver coin.

questions.question: How many coins did the fox collect over the week?
questions.answer: The fox collected five coins over the week.

points.text: The fox collected five coins over the week.

questions.question: Why did the fox like the coins?
questions.answer: The fox liked the coins because they sparkled in the sunlight.

points.text: The fox liked the coins because they sparkled in the sunlight.

questions.question: What part of speech is the word "quiet" in the passage?

points.text: Adjective

questions.question: Change the tense of this sentence to the simple present tense: "The fox collected five coins."

points.text: The fox collects five coins.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with a word from the passage: The fox felt _________ with his new collection.

points.text: happy

questions.question: True or False: The fox knew what the coins were for.

points.text: False

parts.answer: Nouns: fox, stream, food. Verbs: lived, searched, saw.

points.text: Three correct nouns and three correct verbs from the passage.

accept: Any three nouns and any three verbs found in the passage.
scheme.common_error: Words that are not nouns or verbs.

Punctuation.main_question: Rewrite the passage with correct capital letters and punctuation marks.
Punctuation.question: what a lovely morning is pinkys farm far from here rani packed apples pears and plums
Punctuation.answer: What a lovely morning! Is Pinky's farm far from here? Rani packed apples, pears and plums.

points.text: Capital letters used correctly at the start of each sentence and for the names Pinky and Rani
Exclamation mark placed after 'What a lovely morning'
Question mark placed after 'far from here'
Apostrophe used correctly in Pinky's
Commas placed in the list of fruits and a full stop at the end

accept: Commas after apples and pears with 'and' before plums
Comma also placed before 'and' (apples, pears, and plums)
scheme.common_error: Leaving out the apostrophe in Pinky's or using a full stop instead of a question mark or exclamation mark

Word Sentences.main_question: Use any five of the given words in lines of your own. Show clearly what each word means.
Word Sentences.answer:
forgiveness: Saying sorry and getting forgiveness made Ali feel light and happy.
responsibility: Feeding the pet every day is my responsibility.
democracy: In a democracy, people vote to pick their leaders.
ancient: We saw an ancient temple that was thousands of years old.
transformation: A caterpillar goes through a transformation to become a butterfly.
rustle: The dry leaves rustle when the wind blows.

points.text: First word: the line shows the meaning of the word, and the line is correct
Second word: the line shows the meaning of the word, and the line is correct
Third word: the line shows the meaning of the word, and the line is correct
Fourth word: the line shows the meaning of the word, and the line is correct
Fifth word: the line shows the meaning of the word, and the line is correct

accept: Any correct line in which the context makes the meaning of the word clear
scheme.common_error: Writing a line that is grammatically correct but does not show the meaning, e.g. 'I like democracy.'

Rhyming Words.main_question: Read the poem lines. Write two pairs of rhyming words from them.
Rhyming Words.question: City Life vs. Farm Life: A Friendly Debate
Rhyming Words.passage:
Rani replies with a smile so bright,
"But the farm's a peaceful land,
Animals play, fields so grand.
Trees so tall they touch the sky,
Birds and butterflies fly by."
Pinky speaks of urban thrill,
"In the city, there's always play,
Friends and games just steps away.
Sounds of life in every street,
Music plays, a lively beat."

points.text: First rhyming pair written correctly from the lines
Second rhyming pair written correctly from the lines

accept: Any two correct rhyming pairs from the lines, in any order
scheme.common_error: Pairing words that look alike but do not rhyme, or writing only one word from a pair

Mind Map.main_question: Draw a mind map on the topic given below. Draw five branches.
Mind Map.question: Making Chocolate
Mind Map.answer: Cocoa beans; Harvesting; Roasting in a factory; Tempering; Moulding into shapes

points.text: Topic written in the centre of a drawn map
Five branches drawn from the centre
First branch relates correctly to the topic
Second and third branches relate correctly to the topic
Fourth and fifth branches relate correctly to the topic

Application Writing.main_question: Write an application to your principal for sick leave.
Application Writing.question: Write an application to your principal for sick leave.
Application Writing.answer: Correct format: To The Principal, school name, date, subject line (Sick leave), salutation, body saying the student is ill and asks for leave for a stated number of days, polite closing, Yours obediently, name, class.

points.text: Correct format: address to the principal, date and subject
Respectful salutation
Reason for leave (illness) clearly stated
Number of days or dates of leave stated with a polite request
Polite closing, name and class
Correct spelling, capitals and punctuation

accept: Any suitable illness such as fever or stomach ache
Either 'Respected Sir/Madam' or 'Dear Sir/Madam' as a respectful opening
scheme.common_error: Writing in an informal tone or leaving out the subject line and the dates of leave

Application Writing.main_question: Write a letter to your friend telling them about your favourite book.
Application Writing.question: Write a letter to your friend telling them about your favourite book.
Application Writing.answer: Correct letter format: address, date, Dear (friend's name), opening greeting, body naming the book and saying what it is about and why it is liked, closing greeting, Your friend, name.

points.text: Correct letter format: address and date
Greeting and friendly opening
Name of the favourite book given
What the book is about, in a few clear details
Reasons why the book is liked
Friendly closing, 'Your friend' and name
Correct spelling, capitals and punctuation

accept: Any suitable book the child names
scheme.common_error: Writing only about the story with no letter format or no reasons for liking the book

Paragraph Writing.main_question: Write a paragraph of about 8 to 10 lines on any one of the following topics.
Paragraph Writing.answer: A paragraph with a topic sentence, 5 to 7 supporting details with facts and examples, and a concluding sentence.

points.text: A clear topic sentence introducing the chosen topic
Supporting details that stay on the topic
Ideas in a logical order
A concluding sentence
Correct grammar and tense
Correct spelling, capitals and punctuation

accept: Any of the three topics, written with relevant details
scheme.common_error: A list of unconnected sentences with no topic sentence or conclusion

Story Writing.main_question: Complete the story using the outline given below.
Story Writing.question: A boy finds a lost kitten near the park — The kitten is cold and hungry — He takes it home — His mother gives it milk — They put up notices on trees — Days pass and nobody comes — A girl arrives looking for her pet — The boy returns the kitten gladly — The girl thanks him — Moral
Story Writing.answer: A story that follows every cue in order, e.g. the boy finds the kitten, cares for it, searches for the owner and returns it, ending with the moral: Kindness and honesty bring happiness.

points.text: The story follows the outline cues in order
A clear beginning, middle and end with some detail
A suitable moral at the end
Correct tense, spelling and punctuation

accept: Moral: Honesty is the best policy
scheme.common_error: Leaving out the moral or retelling only a few of the cues

Picture Description.main_question: Write 5 to 6 lines about the picture. Use the given words to help you.
Picture Description.question: a busy fruit and vegetable market
Picture Description.describe_en: A busy market stall: a vendor weighing fruits on a scale, baskets of vegetables and fruits, a customer buying, and a crowd of shoppers behind.
Picture Description.answer: This is a busy market. A vendor is weighing fruits for a customer. There are baskets of fresh vegetables near the shop. A crowd of people has come to buy things.

points.text: Description matches the scene shown in the picture
At least five of the given words used correctly
Lines joined in a sensible order
Correct tense, spelling and punctuation

accept: Present continuous or simple present used consistently
Any other correct details about the market scene
scheme.common_error: Writing a list of the given words without making complete lines about the picture

header.title_en: Grade 5 · English · FDE pattern practice paper
header.title_ur: جماعت پنجم · انگریزی · FDE pattern کا مشقی پرچہ
header.note_en: Note: This paper consists of THREE Sections. Section – A needs to be solved on the Question Paper. Sections B & C are to be solved on the Answer Sheet. Cutting, erasing and overwriting is not allowed.

slots.instruction_en: Read each question carefully and choose the correct option. Each question carries 1 mark.

grain.kind: one grammar or vocabulary point per item

slots.prompt_rule: Twenty four-option MCQs, one point each, covering: collective and proper nouns, articles, irregular plurals, antonyms, pronouns, syllables, adverbs, suffixes, tenses, homophones, compound words, degrees of adjectives, modals, apostrophe, spelling, anagrams, sentence types, quantifiers, adjectives. Never refer to an underline the paper cannot show; quote the word instead. An antonym item has one exact opposite among its options.

grain.kind: one-line transformation: rewrite as a simile, identify subject + verb + object, change the tense, simile or metaphor

slots.prompt_rule: Five one-line items, each ending with the direction in round brackets, e.g. "The baby is sleeping. (Change into simple past)". Cover similes/metaphors, S+V+O and simple present/past.

slots.instruction_en: Read the following passage and answer the questions given at the end.

parts_spec.label: iii.
parts_spec.instruction_en: Choose three nouns and three verbs from the given passage.

grain.kind: an unseen narrative passage of about 120 words; five literal or inference questions; four do-as-directed items tied to the passage; three nouns and three verbs

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `passage` = an unseen story of 120–160 words; `parts` = [{key:"questions", questions:[5]}, {key:"do_as_directed", questions:[4: a part of speech of a quoted word, a tense change, a fill-in from the passage, a true/false]}, {key:"pick", pick:{"Nouns":[5 nouns], "Verbs":[5 verbs]}}]. Every picked word is copied exactly as written in the passage, inflection included ("walked", never "walk"); two spares of each kind, the scheme keeps the first three that are in the passage. Never refer to an underlined, bold or italic word; quote the word instead (What part of speech is "quickly"?). A tense rewrite's `accept` never holds another tense.

grain.kind: one or two sentences (about 25 words) with capitals, full stops, a question or exclamation mark, commas and an apostrophe removed

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the unpunctuated passage (lower case, no punctuation), `answer` = the punctuated passage: the printed words exactly, only capitals and punctuation added, nothing reworded, added or dropped; never turn a reported question into direct speech. A points only, one per mark, each for punctuation the printed words can carry (a question mark only where the printed words ask a direct question).

slots.instruction_en: Use any five of the following words in meaningful sentences.

grain.kind: six unit vocabulary words, any five used in sentences

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `words` = exactly six words from units 1–10; `answer` = one model sentence per word, no definitions. 2 marks a word: the sentence shows what the word means 1 + the sentence is correct 1. The paper asks only for sentences, so never ask for, or mark, a written meaning.

slots.instruction_en: Write down FOUR rhyming words from the poem “{q}”

grain.kind: match four cue words to their rhymes in a 9–10 line poem from the book

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the title of a poem from units 1–10 exactly as in the book; `passage` = 6–10 of its lines exactly as printed in the book, holding at least two rhyming pairs; no `words` (the four rhyming words are the answer, so nothing on the paper may list them); `answer` = the four rhyming words as two pairs, each word copied from the passage (e.g. "white – night; wet – yet").

grain.kind: a textbook topic; the child draws a map with five branches

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = a short topic from units 1–10 (2–4 words). The child draws the map; never refer to boxes or branches printed on the paper. `answer` = five possible branches.

grain.kind: a formal application OR an informal letter from FDE's closed lists

slots.prompt_rule: Two items: (a) "Write an application to your principal for …" with a topic from closed_lists.applications; (b) "Write a letter …" with a topic from closed_lists.informal_letters.

slots.instruction_en: Write a paragraph on any ONE of the following topics.

grain.kind: three paragraph topics from FDE's closed list; the child writes one

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `topics` = three different titles from closed_lists.paragraphs, exactly as listed.

slots.instruction_en: Develop a story with a moral from the given outline. Also suggest a suitable title.

grain.kind: an outline of 8–12 cues separated by dashes, ending with "Moral"

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = the outline, 8–12 short cues separated by " — ", ending "— Moral". No title.

slots.instruction_en: Describe the picture with the help of the given word bank. Also suggest a suitable title.

grain.kind: a nine-word bank for an everyday scene (classroom, park, market)

slots.prompt_rule: One item: `question` = a one-line scene for the teacher (e.g. "children painting in an art lesson"), `words` = 8–10 words a child would use to describe that scene. The paper prints a frame and the word bank; a picture of the scene prints in the frame (the teacher adds one if it cannot be drawn). Never describe the picture to the child. `describe_en` = a short English description of the scene that names the things behind the words, drawn as a plain black outline picture in the frame; it is never shown to the child.

frame.title_en: Picture (pasted or drawn by the teacher)

slots.teacher_note_en: Paste or draw a picture that fits the word bank in the frame before photocopying.
